subject: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity & isolation for GridHealth — SLA validation
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Shelly Tran <shelly@gridhealth.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity & isolation for GridHealth — SLA validation

Hi Shelly —

Thanks for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the asks we walked through so we have alignment before we put a formal proposal together. I captured actions below and attached a rough capacity estimate + draft SLA for your procurement/security teams to review.

Key pain points you described
- Production latency spikes during morning batch runs and clinical ingestion peaks (50–80 qps peaks).
- Regulatory requirement: PHI handling; need VPC/private deployment with audited access controls and KMS integration.
- Risk tolerance: want tenant isolation so one team’s model traffic cannot affect other workloads.

Goals you confirmed
- Predictable per-token cost and stable p95 latency under 200ms for inference-critical endpoints.
- 99.9% throughput availability (SLA target) for the dedicated pool; automatic graceful degradation to a smaller/quantized variant during pressure.
- Onboard a two-week POC, then move to reserved capacity commitment if POC meets SLOs.

Redwood recommended configuration (initial proposal)
- Dedicated pool: 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved), configured as an isolated tenant slice.
- Burst policy: allow +50% on short bursts from a shared burst bucket for 48 hours/month.
- Model routing: primary model (quantized for cost) + fallback to high-precision variant; prefix KV caching enabled for stable prompts.
- Security: private deployment (VPC) with SAML, KMS, and SOC2 evidence attachment.

SLA targets discussed
- Uptime: 99.9% monthly for the dedicated pool (operational SLA).
- Latency: p95 < 200ms for 2k token windows under normal load; can escalate to 100ms p95 as an optional premium config.

Open / asks for GridHealth (please reply inline)
1) Confirm priority: is isolation + HIPAA compliance the gating blocker for signing?
2) Procurement timeline: who should I loop in (procurement email) and what is your target commit date for reserved capacity?
3) POC scope: confirm 2-week POC with these KPIs: stability (p95 latency), throughput (sustained qps), and failover behavior (fallback model).

Attachments included: gridhealth_capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx, redwood_sla_draft.pdf, security-evidence-index.docx

Next steps I’ll take:
- Draft a canonical POC plan and runbook for your SRE and security teams.
- Share SOC2 and security evidence index to your security mailbox.
- Schedule a procurement intro for next week if you confirm stakeholders.

If you prefer a short call to walk procurement through the SLA language, Jordan and Ben are available — I’ve cc’d them.

Best,

Irene Choi
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Irene — thanks for the clear recap, this matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- HIPAA/PHI is non-negotiable: we need a private VPC deployment and proof of KMS/HSM integration. Can you confirm Redwood’s key rotation cadence and whether the private deploy package supports FIPS-HSM?
- Procurement: please loop in procurement@gridhealth.ai (I’ve cc’d Tom for visibility). Our procurement team typically needs a three-week review window for SLAs and redlines.
- POC: the 2-week POC is fine but we need a short test harness for our ingestion pipeline (we can share a sanitized dataset). For success, p95 latency < 200ms and no cross-tenant QoS impact are the must-haves.

I’ll review the attachments and get back with any redlines. If you can share SOC2 documentation and a list of exported audit logs, that will speed security review.

Shelly
Head of Platform Engineering
GridHealth
